title: Crisis Communication
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Una crisis mal manejada puede destruir una corporación. Con este vocabulario, sabrás cómo las empresas controlan los daños, emiten comunicados y superan escándalos de relaciones públicas.

stages.title: Comunicación de Crisis y Relaciones Públicas (C2)

parts.visual:
Toda empresa enfrenta escándalos o desastres. El 'PR' (Public Relations) es cómo lo manejan. 

1. Damage control (Control de daños): 
- Las acciones inmediatas para minimizar el impacto negativo de una crisis. 
Ej: The PR team is doing DAMAGE CONTROL after the CEO's offensive tweet. 

2. Backlash (Reacción negativa fuerte): 
- La furia pública contra una decisión de la empresa. 
Ej: We faced a massive BACKLASH when we raised the prices by 50%. 

3. Press release (Comunicado de prensa): 
- Una declaración oficial escrita enviada a los medios de comunicación. 
Ej: We will issue a PRESS RELEASE apologizing for the server outage.
parts.audio: Welcome to Crisis Communication and Public Relations, known as PR. Every company faces scandals or disasters. How they manage it is crucial. Number 1: Damage control. Immediate actions taken to minimize the negative impact of a crisis. For example: The PR team is doing DAMAGE CONTROL after the CEO's offensive tweet. Number 2: Backlash. A strong and negative public reaction against a decision or action. For example: We faced a massive BACKLASH when we raised the prices by 50 percent. Number 3: Press release. An official written statement sent to the media to provide information. For example: We will issue a PRESS RELEASE apologizing for the server outage.

parts.visual:
4. To downplay (Minimizar la importancia): 
- Tratar de hacer que un problema parezca menos grave de lo que es. 
Ej: The company tried to DOWNPLAY the severity of the data breach. 

5. Scapegoat (Chivo expiatorio): 
- Una persona a la que se culpa injustamente para proteger a los verdaderos culpables. 
Ej: The junior developer was used as a SCAPEGOAT for the system failure. 

6. Cover-up (Encubrimiento): 
- Un intento ilegal o antiético de ocultar un error o crimen. 
Ej: The scandal wasn't the mistake itself, it was the COVER-UP. 

7. To clear the air (Aclarar las cosas): 
- Hablar abiertamente para eliminar malentendidos o tensión. 
Ej: We held a town hall meeting to CLEAR THE AIR regarding the rumors.
parts.audio: Number 4: To downplay. Trying to make a problem seem less important or severe than it really is. For example: The company tried to DOWNPLAY the severity of the data breach. Number 5: Scapegoat. A person who is unfairly blamed for something that others have done, to protect the real culprits. For example: The junior developer was used as a SCAPEGOAT for the system failure. Number 6: Cover-up. An unethical or illegal attempt to hide a mistake, crime, or scandal. For example: The scandal wasn't the mistake itself, it was the COVER-UP. Number 7: To clear the air. To speak openly in order to remove tension or misunderstandings. For example: We held a town hall meeting to CLEAR THE AIR regarding the rumors.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término de relaciones públicas correcto.

questions.question: After the defective product caught fire on live TV, the PR team went into immediate ____ control. (Control de daños).
The decision to charge users for previously free features resulted in a massive customer ____. (Reacción negativa furiosa).
questions.explanation: Backlash = reacción negativa fuerte del público.

questions.question: To formally announce the resignation of the CEO to the newspapers, we will issue a ____ release. (Comunicado de prensa).
The executives knew the cars were unsafe, but they tried to ____ the danger in their public statements. (Minimizar la importancia).
questions.explanation: Downplay = restar importancia, minimizar (hacer ver menos grave).

questions.question: The board of directors made the terrible decision, but they fired the marketing manager as a ____ to calm the public. (Chivo expiatorio).
questions.explanation: Scapegoat = chivo expiatorio (a quien se le echa la culpa).

questions.question: The financial fraud was bad, but the illegal ____ orchestrated by the lawyers is what sent them to prison. (Encubrimiento).
There have been many false rumors about layoffs. We need to hold a meeting to ____ the air. (Aclarar las cosas).
questions.explanation: Clear the air = aclarar rumores o aliviar tensiones.

questions.question: When a company tries to make itself look environmentally friendly without actually doing anything, it's called ____-washing.
questions.explanation: Greenwashing = lavado de imagen verde (falsa ecología).

questions.question: The strategy to reverse a negative public image and present a positive one is a PR ____. (Giro/Enfoque manipulado).
questions.explanation: Spin = darle la vuelta a una noticia (manipular el enfoque).

questions.question: A PR professional whose job is specifically to manipulate the media to present a positive 'spin' on events is called a ____ doctor.
questions.explanation: Spin doctor = experto en relaciones públicas que manipula noticias a favor.

questions.question: During a crisis, you must strictly follow the talking ____ provided by the legal department. (Puntos clave a decir).
questions.explanation: Talking points = puntos clave o guion preparado para hablar.

questions.question: The politician refused to answer the journalist's questions, giving only a generic 'no ____' statement. (Sin comentarios).
We are currently dealing with the ____ from the failed merger. (Consecuencias negativas/Radioactividad).
questions.explanation: Fallout = las consecuencias o efectos residuales negativos.

questions.question: To repair his image, the celebrity hired a top PR ____. (Agencia/Firma).
questions.explanation: PR firm = agencia de relaciones públicas.

questions.question: Instead of waiting for the scandal to break in the news, we need to get ____ of the story. (Adelantarse a).
questions.explanation: Get ahead of the story = adelantarse a la noticia (dar tu versión primero).

questions.question: When an employee secretly reports illegal activity within their own company to the authorities, they are a ____. (Denunciante).
To throw someone under the ____ means to selfishly blame them to save yourself. (Echarle la culpa / Tirar bajo el autobús).
questions.explanation: Throw someone under the bus = culpar a otro para salvarse uno mismo.

questions.question: If you speak to a journalist but demand that they do not publish your name, you are speaking off the ____. (Extraoficialmente).
questions.explanation: Off the record = extraoficialmente, sin que se pueda publicar el nombre.

questions.question: A massive, unorganized attack by internet users (often on social media) destroying a brand's reputation is a public ____. (Linchamiento/Indignación).
In a severe crisis, the CEO should issue a public and unconditional ____. (Disculpa).
questions.explanation: Public apology = disculpa pública (debe ser 'unconditional' para funcionar).

questions.question: Doing ____ control. (Control de daños con D)
Face a massive ____. (Reacción negativa furiosa con B)
Issue a ____ release. (Comunicado de prensa con P)
Try to ____ the issue. (Minimizar importancia con D)
He was a ____. (Chivo expiatorio con S)
An illegal ____-up. (Encubrimiento con C)
____ the air. (Aclarar malentendidos con C)
A PR ____ doctor. (Manipulador de noticias con S)
The ____ from the scandal. (Consecuencias residuales con F)
An internal ____. (Denunciante de fraude interno con W)
